fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled frame bytes are passed to the frame parser; the frame header declares nbytes=2560000, chunksize=256000, so nchunks=10.
The frame_len field (big-endian at header offset 16) must equal the input size; our crafted frame sets it to 36967, matching the file size.
frame->sdata points directly at the attacker-controlled input buffer of 36967 bytes; no copy is made.
nbytes=2560000 and chunksize=256000 yield nchunks=10, so the fuzzer loop will call decompress for nchunk=0.

fine_trace.code: dsize = blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk(schunk, nchunk, uncompressed_data + i, schunk->chunksize);
fine_trace.note: The loop runs for nchunk=0 (since nchunks=10, loop condition nchunk < 9), invoking decompression of chunk 0.

fine_trace.code: chunksize = frame_decompress_chunk(schunk->dctx, schunk->frame, nchunk, dest, nbytes);
fine_trace.note: Since schunk->frame is non-NULL (frame-backed schunk), the call is forwarded to frame_decompress_chunk.
frame_get_lazychunk is called to obtain the compressed chunk pointer and its size.

fine_trace.code: int64_t offset = get_coffset(frame, header_len, cbytes, nchunk);
fine_trace.note: The chunk offset for nchunk=0 is read from the compressed offsets chunk stored in the frame.
blosc_getitem decompresses the offsets chunk and extracts the int64 offset for chunk 0; the attacker-controlled offsets chunk decompresses to offset=36876.
With header_len=92 and offset=36876, *chunk = frame->sdata + 36968, which is 1 byte past the end of the 36967-byte input buffer.
sw32_ reads 4 bytes at *chunk + 12 = frame->sdata + 36980, which is 13 bytes past the end of the heap allocation, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
